name: Stylam Industries Ltd
tagline: Debt-free laminates exporter now controlled by Japan's AICA Kogyo (40% promoter stake, deal closed June 2026); FY26 growth cooled to 10% but Q1 FY27 re-accelerated at record 21% margins as a delayed capacity-doubling plant nears start-up
business_overview: High-pressure decorative laminates manufacturer operating Asia's largest laminate manufacturing plant, with roughly 64-72% of revenue historically from exports; expanding into acrylic solid-surface and MDF-board lamination adjacencies. Japan's AICA Kogyo became the largest shareholder / promoter with a 40% stake (closed June 2026) and has nominated 8 of the board's directors.
fundamentals_table: FY26 Rs 1,129 Cr (+10% YoY, down from ~17% CAGR); Q1 FY27 Rs 326 Cr (+15% YoY, +15% QoQ)
~13% (FY26 PAT Rs 150 Cr, +23% YoY); Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin >21% (record)
Almost debt-free (Rs 29 Cr borrowings Mar 2026); FY26 CFO Rs 177 Cr = ~104% of EBITDA
fundamentals_narrative: Revenue CAGR of ~19% over 5 years with a debt-free balance sheet and ~20% ROE, but the deep dive shows FY26 growth decelerated sharply to 10% (Rs 1,129 Cr) before Q1 FY27 re-accelerated to +15% YoY on record >21% EBITDA margins and +70% YoY PAT. Cash conversion is strong and improving (FY26 CFO Rs 177 Cr, ~104% of EBITDA, vs ~82-83% in FY24/FY25). The AICA Kogyo transaction - the core catalyst - is now closed: AICA holds 40% as promoter, has 8 board nominees, and an open offer at Rs 2,250 (well below CMP) completed in May 2026 with only ~2.75% tendered. The new Panchkula plant has slipped twice (June 2026 -> Sept 1, 2026 commercial start), capex raised to Rs 200-225 Cr (extra line), funded internally; it is guided to add Rs 250-300 Cr revenue in year 1 at 25-30% utilisation. Domestic operations (the loss-making leg) are being restructured with a swing to profit expected from Q3 FY27.
technical_read: Not independently pulled this pass. Stock trades near its 52-week high (~Rs 3,508 vs high Rs 3,509) after a ~2.2x re-rating over the year, so the AICA catalyst and margin step-up are substantially in the price.
sentiment_summary: Read most recent 50 of 130 posts (Dec 2021 to June 2026), spanning years of consistent 15-30%+ quarterly growth through the laminate cycle, a promoter-family-dispute disclosure, and the AICA Kogyo transaction. Deep dive (pass 1) cross-checked against FY26 audited results, the Q1 FY27 concall, and BSE/NSE filings through Aug 2026.
community_signal: harsh.beria93 and ranvir (both trusted) provided detailed multi-year concall coverage showing consistent 15-30%+ revenue growth, with management repeatedly raising long-term capacity/revenue targets (Rs 1,000 Cr -> Rs 1,500 Cr -> Rs 1,800-2,000 Cr). Most significant: Dec 2025/Mar 2026 posts confirm Japan's AICA Kogyo is acquiring a controlling stake, alongside resolution of a multi-year promoter-family dispute (nephew Manav Gupta's exit) that had specifically bottlenecked the domestic business. Deep dive confirms the deal closed (40% AICA promoter stake, June 2026) - the governance overhang is resolved, but the open offer priced at Rs 2,250 is far below the market price, so there is no takeout premium for minority holders.
bse_notes: Board reconstituted 17 June 2026: 8 new AICA-nominated directors on 5-year terms. AGM 28 Aug 2026 sought approval for revised managerial remuneration post-partnership. Open offer (26% sought at Rs 2,250) closed May 2026 with only ~4.66 lakh shares (~2.75%) tendered; AICA topped up to 40% via off-market blocks on 17 June 2026. No adverse rating action, litigation or auditor issue surfaced.
bull_case: ~19% 5-yr revenue CAGR, ROE ~20%, ROCE 26.6%, essentially debt-free, and FY26 cash conversion of ~104% of EBITDA - a genuinely high-quality compounder
Q1 FY27 inflection: revenue +15% YoY, EBITDA margin a record >21% (vs 19-20% guided), PAT +70% YoY - growth and margins both re-accelerating after a flat FY26

AICA Kogyo (Japanese laminates major) control is now closed and de-risked - promoter overhang and the multi-year family dispute are both resolved, with potential access to AICA technology, products and global distribution as unpriced optionality
New Panchkula plant (commercial start Sept 2026, Rs 200-225 Cr capex, self-funded) adds Rs 250-300 Cr of revenue in year 1 (~22-27% of FY26 sales) with room to scale as utilisation rises
bear_case: FY26 revenue grew only 10% (Rs 1,129 Cr) - a sharp deceleration from the ~17-19% CAGR narrative; the Q1 FY27 re-acceleration is one quarter old and unconfirmed

Stock is at its 52-week high after a ~2.2x re-rating on ~35x trailing P/E and ~7.4x P/B - the AICA catalyst and margin step-up are largely priced in; the Rs 2,250 open offer sits far below CMP, so no downside cushion from a takeout floor
New plant has slipped twice (June -> Sept 2026) and capex was raised mid-project; year-1 utilisation is only 25-30%, so the earnings contribution is back-ended into FY28
Domestic segment is still loss-making; the turnaround is an in-progress restructuring, not a delivered result, with benefits only from Q3 FY27
AICA now controls the board and is seeking revised managerial remuneration - minority holders are a passenger to a foreign strategic promoter's capital-allocation and related-party decisions
verdict_headline: High-quality debt-free compounder with a now-closed strategic-investor catalyst and a fresh Q1 FY27 inflection - but full valuation at the highs caps it below top conviction
verdict_reasoning: Deep dive confirms the fundamentals (cash-backed FY26, record Q1 FY27 margins, pristine balance sheet) and de-risks the catalyst (AICA deal closed, governance overhang gone)
But FY26 growth decelerated to 10%, the capacity catalyst has slipped twice and is back-ended, and the stock sits at its 52-week high on ~35x earnings - the easy part of the re-rating is done
A literal 10x in 2-3 years from a Rs 5,945 Cr base is a stretch; this is better read as a Medium-High-conviction quality compounder with a real but partly-priced capacity + AICA optionality kicker

sources_reviewed: FY26 audited results + FY24/FY25 comparatives via screener.in and press (revenue, PAT, net worth, borrowings, cash flow)
Q1 FY27 results + earnings-call highlights (Jul 2026): revenue Rs 326 Cr, EBITDA >21%, PAT Rs 48 Cr, plant/margin/domestic guidance
BSE/NSE announcements Feb-Aug 2026: AICA open offer close, 40% stake completion, board reconstitution, AGM remuneration resolution
annual_report_findings: FY26 revenue Rs 1,129 Cr, up only ~10% YoY (FY25 Rs 1,025 Cr, FY24 Rs 914 Cr, FY23 Rs 952 Cr) - materially slower than the ~17-19% CAGR in the prior write-up
FY26 PAT Rs 150 Cr (+23% YoY), EPS ~Rs 88; net worth Rs 807 Cr (+22.75%); borrowings cut to ~Rs 29 Cr - effectively debt-free
FY26 operating cash flow Rs 177 Cr = ~104% of EBITDA, up from ~82-83% conversion in FY24 and FY25 - working capital discipline improved, growth is cash-backed
ROCE 26.6%, ROE 19.9% - sustained high-teens/20s returns with no leverage
Capex for the new Panchkula plant raised to Rs 200-225 Cr (additional line installed), self-funded from internal accruals
quarterly_trend: Quarterly revenue: Jun'25 283 / Sep'25 292 / Dec'25 271 / Mar'26 283 / Jun'26 326 Cr - flat through FY26, then a clear step-up in Q1 FY27
Q1 FY27: revenue +15.4% YoY and +15% QoQ; EBITDA margin >21% (record, management calls it operational efficiency not inventory gains); PAT Rs 48 Cr, +70% YoY
Management guides sustainable EBITDA margin 19-20% even as the new capex adds depreciation; Q1 already above that
Domestic business still loss-making; restructuring (team, distributors, warehousing) underway, swing to profit expected from Q3 FY27
recent_announcements: AICA Kogyo open offer (26% at Rs 2,250) closed May 2026 - only ~2.75% tendered; AICA then lifted holding to 40% via off-market blocks on 17 June 2026 and is classified as promoter
Board reconstituted 17 June 2026 with 8 AICA-nominated directors on 5-year terms
AGM 28 Aug 2026: resolutions for revised managerial remuneration following the AICA partnership
New Panchkula plant commercial production pushed from June 2026 to 1 September 2026 (internal + weather delays); year-1 revenue guided Rs 250-300 Cr at 25-30% utilisation
key_new_facts: AICA Kogyo deal is CLOSED (40% promoter stake, board control) - the catalyst is now a fact, not a pending event; open offer price Rs 2,250 is far below CMP so no minority takeout premium
FY26 organic growth was only ~10%, well below the narrative - the thesis now rests on the Q1 FY27 re-acceleration holding
New plant delayed a second time to Sept 2026 and capex raised; earnings contribution is back-ended to FY28
FY26 cash conversion actually strong (~104% of EBITDA) - quality of earnings confirmed
open_questions: Is the Q1 FY27 +15% revenue / 21% margin step-up sustainable, or partly a one-quarter phasing/price effect?
What concrete commercial synergies (products, tech, export channels) will AICA bring, and on what timeline - nothing quantified yet
How will AICA-controlled board handle capital allocation, dividends and related-party purchases from the parent?
Will the Panchkula plant actually start on 1 Sept 2026 after two slips, and how fast does utilisation ramp?
deep_dive.conviction_update: High -> Medium-High. The filings confirm a high-quality, cash-backed, debt-free compounder and de-risk the AICA catalyst (deal closed), but they also reveal FY26 growth decelerated to 10%, the capacity catalyst has slipped twice and is back-ended, and the stock is at its 52-week high on ~35x earnings with the open offer well below CMP - the re-rating has largely happened, so top conviction is no longer warranted.

earnings_chain.operating_leverage: yes - Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin >21% vs 19-20% guided; management expects to hold margins even as new capex adds depreciation, implying EBITDA can grow at least in line with revenue

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: ~35x trailing P/E on a debt-free ~20% ROE compounder implies roughly 18-22% EPS CAGR FY26-FY28 against a ~22-25x normal exit multiple - the market is pricing the new-plant ramp and a margin hold, but not a step-change or large AICA synergy
market_expectation.our_fy27_estimate: Revenue +15-20% (Q1 +15%, new plant only a partial year), EBITDA margin ~20-21%, PAT +25-35% off the low FY26 base plus the margin step-up
market_expectation.our_fy28_estimate: second leg as Panchkula utilisation rises past 30% and domestic swings to profit - revenue toward Rs 1,600-1,800 Cr, PAT ~Rs 230-260 Cr
market_expectation.gap_basis: new Panchkula capacity (Rs 250-300 Cr year-1, more as utilisation scales) and record ~21% margins are only partly in a 35x multiple that already sits at a 52-week high; AICA commercial synergies are unpriced optionality with no numbers yet
market_expectation.data_caveat: no broker consensus; implied path is a reverse-P/E estimate + screener.in forward figures + VP thread view

catalyst.event: Panchkula plant commercial start (Sep 2026) plus Q2/Q3 FY27 prints showing new-capacity revenue, sustained ~20% margins, and the domestic segment swinging to profit from Q3 FY27

four_box.note: Capacity/AICA-led growth, not a clear macro tailwind; verdict explicitly says literal 10x from Rs5,945Cr base 'is a stretch'; no moat data; 35x P/E at 52-wk high, 'easy part of re-rating is done' [audit 2026-09-07: thesis_fit set to 'neither' to satisfy the four_box <=1.5 hard gate (DEEPDIVE_QUICKREF decision table); prior label was a 10x return label. vpscreen-rerank may revisit if boxes improve.]
